subject: c12-eng

weightage.label: Literature Text Book and Supplementary Reading Text

note: Official CBSE theory paper: 80 marks. Reading Skills = 22, Creative Writing Skills = 18, Literature Text Book and Supplementary Reading Text = 40. Internal assessment is separate: Listening 5, Speaking 5 and Project Work 10.
mistakes: Reading: answering from general knowledge instead of the passage; support answers with evidence from the given text.
Reading: confusing inference with a sentence copied from the passage; state the inference clearly and connect it to the textual evidence.
Creative writing: losing marks through incorrect format, missing required parts, weak organisation, or ignoring the requested word range.
Creative writing: using memorised content that does not address the specific verbal/visual input.
Literature: retelling the whole chapter instead of answering the exact analytical or inferential question.
Literature: writing character/theme claims without linking them to a relevant incident, image, line, or event from the text.
Poetry: identifying a poetic device without explaining its effect or connection to meaning.
Long answers: spending too much space on introduction and not developing the analytical or evaluative response.
order: Finish the two reading-skill formats first: unseen passage and case-based factual passage; practise extracting evidence and making concise inferences.
Build a reliable writing-format checklist for notice, invitation/reply, letter, article and report; practise within the prescribed word ranges.
Read Flamingo prose and poetry actively: theme, central idea, important incidents/images, characterisation and likely inferential links.
Read Vistas for global comprehension; track each chapter's central conflict, turning points and themes rather than memorising summaries.
Practise mixed literature questions only after the texts are understood; prioritise analytical and inferential answers.
Finish with timed full-section practice and review errors by category: comprehension, format, expression, evidence and interpretation.
